paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Saul's trouble wasn't the Philistines. It was the waiting. Samuel had told him to wait seven days, and when Samuel didn't show, Saul looked at his shrinking troops and decided he couldn't hold out any longer. So he offered the burnt offering himself. I know that pressure, friend. I've stared at an oven timer like it owed me money.

Now listen to what Samuel says, because this is the heart of it. Saul said he felt compelled, and Samuel told him, "You have acted foolishly." Saul had not kept the command the LORD gave him (1 Samuel 13:13). His fear was real, and I think the pressure felt heavy. But feeling like you have to doesn't change what God said. Saul looked at his troops, the Philistines and the clock, and he stopped looking at the command.

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery today. When God's timing feels slow and everything around you is scattering, that's the moment to stay with what He said, not rush ahead of it. Saul lost his kingdom over this, because the LORD had sought "a man after His own heart" (1 Samuel 13:14). That's a big deal, so don't skip it. And keep your apron on, friend, because this story isn't over.
